title: How to Hold a Guitar: Posture, Leg Position, and Arm Support (JustinGuitar)
summary: This instructional video guides a beginner through practical guitar holding and posture to minimize strain and facilitate chord changes. Justin explains a right-handed player should typically place the guitar on the right leg (with an optional left-leg classical setup), how the forearm should rest and support the guitar rather than the shoulder bearing the weight, and the importance of relaxing the arm to avoid fatigue. He notes differences for acoustic (forearm sits on top) versus electric (forearm rests on the front), and suggests sleeves or fabric can affect grip. A stable, cutaway–torso interaction helps the instrument stay in place, while not leaning across the neck and maintaining an upright posture reduces risk of wrist, neck, and back discomfort. The narrative also covers practical cautions such as avoiding leaning to look at fingers, and the possibility of using a strap as an alternative support.

sections.description: Justin recommends placing the guitar on the right leg for right-handed players, with a note that a left-leg classical setup is possible but offers limited beginner benefits. The forearm should touch the guitar rather than the shoulder bearing most of the weight. For acoustic guitars the forearm sits on the top; for electrics it rests on the front, with a light grip. The guitar should be held by the arm, with the cutaway resting on the leg or a strap, and not supported by the hand on the neck.

sections.description: The presenter cautions against leaning the guitar to view the fretboard, which can force the wrist into an awkward position and elevate injury risk. He emphasizes maintaining an upright posture to protect the back and neck, and acknowledges that beginners may still crane their neck a little, but should strive to reduce it for longer-term comfort.
